knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Break-even jobs equal fixed costs per month divided by contribution per job, where contribution is price minus variable cost. Revenue per staff member, price times hours and total wages plus rent do not give the break-even volume.
Cash planning uses the conservative case so the business can survive a slower start. The base case is kept for comparison and the best case is not used for cash decisions.
A profit target is an aim. A forecast needs job counts, costs, hours and timing that show how the aim could be reached.

practicalCriteria: Break-even jobs per month are calculated from the learner's own fixed costs and contribution per job, rounded up.
The stage forecast has base, conservative and upside cases, each with jobs per week and stated assumptions.
A monthly cash-flow table uses the conservative case, with invoice and payment dates.
passRule: Knowledge checks: 80 per cent pass mark (all 3 of 3 correct for this lesson). A quiz pass is not verified practical competence. The break-even worksheet and stage forecast are assessed separately by an assessor against the practical criteria.
evidenceRequired: Break-even worksheet and stage forecast reviewed by an assessor
stopWorkCriteria: Stop committing spend on staff or equipment on the base case alone where the cash-flow table shows a shortfall under the conservative case.
